errata.reason: The POH prints 610 ft/NM, more than the 603 ft/NM it prints 2000 ft lower, though gradient falls with altitude everywhere else in the table. Its neighbours agree on about 510: the column falls 93 ft/NM from 10,000 ft and 88 ft/NM to 14,000 ft (603 and 422), and the row runs about 41 ft/NM above the 0 °C cell (469), as the rows above and below it do. 610 reads as a misprinted 510.
sources: Cirrus POH 13772-001 Rev A10, Figure 5-12

notes.subject: takeoff and landing corrections
notes.text: Wind factors are fractions of distance per 10 knots, from the POH's 10% per 12 knots of takeoff headwind, 10% per 13 knots of landing headwind and 10% per 2 knots of tailwind; the tailwind correction covers up to 10 knots. Slope, grass and air conditioner corrections are stated against the ground roll, and the POH adds the same change in feet to the total distance. Slope factors are fractions of ground roll per 1% of slope, varying with pressure altitude for takeoff.

notes.subject: enroute climb
notes.text: Enroute climb gradient and rate come from the Hartzell supplement whenever the composite propeller is installed, with or without turbonormalizing. The POH approves only metal propellers, so the composite propeller is approved only through 13772-129, which replaces exactly these tables and requires their higher climb speeds for engine cooling. Tornado Alley prints no climb gradient or rate tables of its own and refers to the basic AFM, which includes the installed supplements. The Hartzell tables are also the conservative choice.
sources: Cirrus POH supplement 13772-129 Rev 2, pp. 4-6
Tornado Alley Turbo Report 215-6 Reissue 3, p. 26
FAA AC 20-188 ¶5–7.5 (https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_20-188.pdf)

notes.subject: time, fuel and distance to climb
notes.text: The POH table applies, but it assumes 91-101 KIAS, below the 102-112 KIAS the composite propeller needs for cooling. The Hartzell supplement doesn't replace it, so treat its figures as optimistic.
